Maintenance Report — MNT-0009-003

Asset: WELL-0009 (SW-23 Well 009, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 19 May 2023 08:00 · Finished: 20 May 2023 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 18 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0009-0030 on 2023-05-18 Report written: 22 May 2023

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0009-0030 at 14:15 on 2023-05-18 found crude oil on the pad: about 5.6% of the pad area, estimated 2.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.1 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 389 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 311 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.0 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0009-003 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.52% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0009-016

Asset: WELL-0009 (SW-23 Well 009, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 22 Mar 2025 08:00 · Finished: 30 Apr 2025 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 938 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0009-0125 on 2025-03-20 Report written: 01 May 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw a thin film of oil on the wellhead. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0009-0125 showed the wellhead at 19.7 °C with the air at 13.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 37 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Packing wear sped up by a slightly misaligned polished rod.

Safety and permits

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Maintenance Report — MNT-0009-021

Asset: WELL-0009 (SW-23 Well 009, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 14 Sep 2025 08:00 · Finished: 16 Sep 2025 14:00 · Well stopped for this job: 54 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0009-0149 on 2025-09-11 Report written: 16 Sep 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0009-0149 showed the wellhead at 37.9 °C with the air at 29.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.
